newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - dampened by futures rally.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - dampened by futures rally.

text.p: Surging prices on the futures market and firm differentials kept roasters away from the New York physical coffee market this week despite their dwindling inventories, traders said.
"Nobody wants to offer physicals until this market settles down," a trader said. "Roasters missed the boat. They expected differentials to go down with more coffee coming in, but where's the coffee?"
A dockworkers strike in second-largest producer Colombia delayed shipment of some 300,000 60-kg bags of coffee and rattled a market already worried about tight prompt supplies.

Although the dockworkers returned to work on Friday, traders said the resumption of coffee shipments out of Colombia was unlikely to pressure differentials -- or alleviate the supply crunch any time soon.

Heightening the supply concerns this week was news the Association of Coffee Producing Countries agreed to cut in coffee exports by 1.3 million bags between January and June 1997, including 300,000 bags of arabica beans.
Traders said already hefty spot differentials refused to budge despite the CSCE's March contract 12.90 cents -- or more than 10 percent -- gain on the week.

Colombian MAMs for spot delivery netted 23-27 cents over "C" this week, little changed compared with last week. Spot Santos 4s were offered at two cents under CSCE March, while Santos 2/3s fetched four cents over "C".
However, spot Mexican beans, which substituted for strike-delayed Colombians, firmed this week. Mexicans netted one to two cents under "C", up from three cents under last week.
CSCE March coffee fell 3.15 cents a lb Friday to settle at 136.90. March ended 3.75 lower at 131.30.
